name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; mines and attacks
summary: Hormuz largely shut after mine strikes on tankers on 1 Nov; Iran ties reopening to blockade
state: Iran's IRGC said on 1 Nov that two tankers on an unauthorised route struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, after attacks on tankers on 30–31 Oct (gCaptain). On 2 Nov Iran's foreign ministry said the strait would not reopen until the US lifts its naval blockade; a Qatari-mediated plan could reopen it within two days if accepted. Drones hit at least seven cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria in October.
for_you: Shipping delays and higher freight and insurance costs feed through to fuel and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded with attacks on shipping = Alert

sources.title: gCaptain — Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
ANI — Iran demands end to US naval blockade before any agreement on Strait of Hormuz
Al Jazeera — Iran war live: Tehran says Hormuz 'security restored' if US agrees to plan

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
